title: Kernel + Scheduler + KV Compatibility: INT8/GPTQ/AWQ Constraints (notes)
content:
Context
This is a working note capturing compatibility constraints and pragmatic constraints we need to encode in the runtime when choosing execution kernels, how the scheduler should treat quantized models (INT8/GPTQ/AWQ/FP8), and the interactions with the KV cache. Purpose is to be a lightweight single-source-of-truth for engineers implementing the low-precision execution path and the scheduler fallback logic.

Executive summary / TL;DR
- Not all quantized kernels are drop-in compatible with our standard batching and KV cache semantics.
- We must encode kernel capabilities (allowed seq-len, KV layout, batch alignment, prefetch needs) into a capability matrix consumed by the scheduler.
- Fallback policy: try preferred quant kernel -> compatible reduced-batch path -> higher-precision kernel (INT8->FP16) for correctness over latency.
- KV cache representation must be versioned per-kernel ABI. Runtime will reject KV blobs that don’t match kernel ABI to avoid silent corruption.

Goals
1) Define clear kernel contracts so scheduler and KV cache share a common language (capabilities + restrictions).
2) Minimize runtime surprises when models are served with mixed quant variants.
3) Keep fast path as aggressive as possible for INT8/AWQ where it is safe; provide deterministic fallback strategies for corner cases.

Key definitions
- kernel ABI: the interface expectations for memory layout, alignment, and data type for weights and KV cache.
- capability flags: small structured list learned by runtime at model load (e.g., supports-prefetch, kv-layout=interleaved, max-block-size=64).
- compatible path: an execution path that does not require weight re-conversion and shares the same KV ABI.

Kernel capability matrix (conceptual fields runtime must expose per-model/variant)
- quant-format: {INT8, GPTQ, AWQ, FP8, FP16}
- weight-packing: {none, packed-4x, packed-8x}
- kv-precision: {fp16, int8-encoded, mixed}
- kv-layout: {separate-kv, interleaved, tiled}
- max-seq: integer
- supports-prefetch: boolean
- requires-batch-multiple: integer (e.g., 8 -> input batch dims must be multiple-of-8 for kernel vectorization)
- supports-variable-seqlen: boolean
- fallback-cost-id: small label used by scheduler to pick secondary path

Common constraints discovered (examples from protos and microbenchmarks)
1) Many GPTQ/AWQ kernels currently expect packed weight layouts where Q/K/V matmuls are optimized but require 64-byte alignment and batch-size multiple of 4 for warp-friendly execution. If input batch not aligned, kernel falls back to scalar loop and latency spikes 2.5x.
2) INT8 kernels that use per-row scale require KV cache to be kept in fp16 during decode step (we convert on read). That conversion costs ~0.6us per token per beam on A100 microbench.
3) FP8 kernels with tensor cores prefer fixed tile sizes (e.g., MxK multiples). They are incompatible with our existing tiled KV layout, so we must either transform KV on-the-fly (expensive) or disallow FP8 in mixed KV caches.
4) Some AWQ kernels do not support attention rotary embeddings higher than 64-dim block and will silently glitch for models using larger rotary windows. Kernel capability must advertise max-rotary-dim.

KV cache compatibility rules (runtime policy proposals)
- KV blocks tagged with kernel ABI version (string) at store time. When scheduler selects a kernel, it compares the ABI tag. If mismatch -> reject fast path and either: (a) convert KV on-the-fly (costly), or (b) fall back to different kernel that matches ABI. We prefer (b) unless conversion is within threshold.
- Allow read-only conversion path for short prefixes (<= 8 tokens) where conversion cost < 10ms. For long prefixes prefer full-domain fallback.
- When storing KV blobs for dedicated GPU pools, pin ABI to pool to avoid cross-pool mismatches. Add a per-pool capability fingerprint.

Scheduler interactions and policies
- At model-load, inspect model variant and record kernel capabilities. This becomes part of the routing policy used by the scheduler.
- Routing decision tree (simplified):
  1) Preferred variant available in region/pool? -> check capability match with request (batch size, seq len, rotary dim) -> if yes route.
  2) If mismatch and conversion possible within budget -> schedule conversion job then route.
  3) Else try next-compatible variant (e.g., INT8->FP16) and annotate cost penalty.
- Batching impact: kernels that require batch multiple >1 must be given scheduling preference windows to accumulate inputs; otherwise, schedule smaller batch on fallback kernel. Use dynamic backoff timebox to avoid user-visible latency regressions.

Prefetch and memory considerations
- Some quant kernels rely on weight-prefetch into L2/SM cache. Mark those kernels as supports-prefetch=true and add prefetch budget to scheduling decisions. Prefetch increases per-request memory pressure: runtime must track prefetch residency by GPU and apply eviction when > 80% of prefetched budgets used.
- Memory alignment constraints are critical: if weight-packing requires 64B alignment, we must enforce an allocator path that gives aligned allocations for model weights and KV pages. Failure mode: silent correctness bugs.

Fallback strategies (ordered by preference)
1) Compatible quant kernel with same ABI and acceptable batch/seq -> fast path.
2) Compatible quant kernel with same ABI but requires a reduced batch-size alignment -> route with forced batching window (small delay acceptable for throughput jobs).
3) Non-ABI kernel with on-the-fly KV conversion if estimated cost < threshold.
4) FP16/FP32 kernel (higher precision) as last resort for correctness. Prefer this for low QPS/high SLAs.

Testing and validation plan
- Create a test matrix runner that exercises all combinations of:
  - quant-format x batch-sizes x seq-lens x rotary-dims x kv-layout
  - verify bit-exact behavior where expected, otherwise verify statistically (logit distribution/diff) for quant variants
- Add CI microbench that measures conversion cost between KV ABIs (int8->fp16, fp16->fp8) and report 95p latency.
- Fuzz KV cache loader: randomly corrupt ABI tag and ensure loader rejects with clear error code and telemetry event.

Safety and observability
- Emit a telemetry event when ABI mismatch encountered: include requested kernel, stored KV ABI, estimated conversion cost, and chosen fallback. This helps tune thresholds.
- Add route-level annotation in Console showing: current kernel variant, ABI tag, any conversions performed, and token-level latency delta vs baseline.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to represent mixed-precision KV layouts where some layers store int8 and others fp16? Proposal: per-layer kv-layout metadata, but scheduler complexity increases. Need to prototype.
- Should we store a canonical, portable KV representation (fp16) for long-lived caches and derive quantized views per-kernel on load? Tradeoffs: storage vs conversion CPU/GPU cost.
- Define ABI version naming convention (semver-like?) and compatibility rules. Can a minor bump be backward-compatible? We need clear rules.
- Perf experiments: measure on V100 vs A100 vs H100 for AWQ and GPTQ kernels and update thresholds.

Action items (owners)
- [Asha] prototype ABI tagging + rejection flow in loader (INF-1423).
- [Diego] add capability descriptor to model-load API and persist to model metadata.
- [Priya] run conversion-cost microbench on H100 and report numbers for FP8 <-> FP16 on 2025-01-30.
- [Evan] implement telemetry event + Console annotations for ABI mismatches.

Notes to self
- Keep this doc intentionally informal. Once we converge on ABI fields, move to a formal "kernel-capability-spec" in Confluence. Link: CONFLUENCE-RT/quantization-playbook.
- Expect iterative changes as AWQ/GPTQ kernels evolve; design the runtime to be extensible rather than hardcoded flags.

End of notes.
